s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower extremity edema with acute altered mental status and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Symmetric lower extremity edema
Hepatomegaly and ascites
Severe liver injury with elevated AST and ALT
Hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow
Extensive bilateral femoral-popliteal and iliac vein thrombosis
key_facts: 60-year-old man with hypertension and Parkinson’s disease
3 months of progressive lower extremity edema
Acute onset of altered mental status
Somnolent and disoriented on admission
Symmetric lower extremity edema on examination
Hepatomegaly and ascites without stigmata of chronic liver disease
AST 3877 U/L and ALT 2939 U/L
Total bilirubin 4.5 mg/dL and INR 3.8
White blood cell count 19.4×10^3/μL and platelets 63×10^3/μL
Lactic acid 13.9 mmol/L and BUN 67 mg/dL
Creatinine 3.3 mg/dL
Negative acetaminophen level and toxicology screen
Negative viral hepatitis panels, Epstein–Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and HIV testing
Diagnostic paracentesis negative for infection or malignancy
Hepatic ultrasonography with Doppler showed hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow

shortlist.label: Budd-Chiari syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow

shortlist.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Directly mentioned in key facts and supported by hepatic ultrasonography with Doppler

shortlist.label: Tumor thrombus
shortlist.why_kept: Large echodense mass in the right atrium with preserved left ventricular function and cardiac MRI showing a heterogeneous pericardial mass invading the right atrium

shortlist.label: Inferior vena cava thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive bilateral femoral–popliteal and iliac vein thrombosis and clot burden preventing IVC filter placement

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Heterogeneous pericardial mass invading the right atrium, potentially explaining the tumor thrombus and multi-organ dysfunction

raw.rationale: The presence of a large echodense mass in the right atrium with preserved left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography and a 10.6×5.0×5.6-cm heterogeneous pericardial mass invading the right atrium on cardiac MRI, along with hepatic vein thrombosis and reversal of portal venous flow, suggests a tumor thrombus as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Budd-Chiari syndrome
rejected.why: While hepatic vein thrombosis is present, the presence of a large mass in the right atrium and pericardial invasion suggests a more complex diagnosis than Budd-Chiari syndrome alone.

rejected.label: Hepatic vein thrombosis
rejected.why: Hepatic vein thrombosis is a component of the presentation, but it does not fully explain the large mass in the right atrium and pericardial invasion.

rejected.label: Inferior vena cava thrombosis
rejected.why: Although thrombosis is present, the primary issue appears to be related to a tumor thrombus rather than isolated inferior vena cava thrombosis.

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoma
rejected.why: While the mass could be a cardiac sarcoma, the term 'tumor thrombus' more specifically describes the combination of tumor and thrombosis seen in this patient's presentation.
